$comment: Project settings for glpnet. Checked in, so every session in this repo inherits them.
THE /btw HOOK (M6-f). Engineer ruling R-C (2026-09-05) requires the engineer's explicit
consent before a lane installs this, and the harness refuses it otherwise. Consent was given
on 2026-09-05 for the PROJECT settings, not settings.local.json, so the fleet can verify from
the repo that this lane's M6 alert half is actually wired rather than taking a claim on trust.
WHAT IT DOES. The code-based YNET client (csharp/ynet_client) receives with no agent attached
and records every alert durably. It cannot reach the agent's process at all - by construction
it holds no pid, no pipe and no handle (093 FR-008) - so something on the agent's own side has
to look. This UserPromptSubmit hook looks at a genuine turn boundary and prints what is
pending, which is the /btw semantic: the agent is OFFERED work and chooses interrupt-or-defer,
never interrupted mid-tool-call, and an absent or busy agent can neither block receipt nor
WHY IT IS SAFE. The hook is fail-silent by design: any error at all exits 0 with no output,
and its output is capped so a flooded alert directory cannot flood the agent's context. A
broken hook must never be able to disrupt the prompt path - the hook is a convenience, the
prompt is the product. To remove it, delete the hooks block; nothing else depends on it.
